question: What are the requirements for an egress window in a basement bedroom?
reference_answer: Every floor level containing a bedroom in a suite needs at least one outside window that is openable from the inside without tools, provides an unobstructed open portion of at least 0.35 m2 with no dimension less than 380 mm, and maintains that opening without additional support (OBC 9.9.10.1). Basement windows are exempt from the 1,000 mm maximum sill height, and a window opening into a window well needs at least 550 mm of clearance in front of it.
notes: Eval Q3/Q7 anchor; guideline S7 code-trigger checklist maps basement bedroom to 9.9.10.

question: Where are carbon monoxide alarms required in a house with a basement apartment?
reference_answer: OBC 9.32.3.9/9.32.3.9A: a CO alarm is required in a residential suite where a fuel-burning appliance or flue is in the suite, where a forced-air fuel-burning appliance heats the suite, or where the suite shares a wall/floor/ceiling assembly with a room containing a fuel-burning appliance or with a storage garage. Inside the suite, alarms go adjacent to each sleeping room and on each storey without one. Note the 2024 numbering: CO alarms are 9.32.3.9, not the old 9.33.4.
notes: Numbering gotcha from CLAUDE.md; two matchers because 9.32.3.9A is a sibling article, not a child.

question: Do I need interconnected smoke alarms when adding a basement suite?
reference_answer: OBC 9.10.19 requires smoke alarms in each dwelling unit and in ancillary and common spaces of a house with a secondary suite. Within a dwelling unit there must be at least one alarm per storey including the basement, one in each sleeping room, and one between the sleeping rooms and the rest of the storey; in a house with a secondary suite, shared means of egress and common areas each need an alarm, with visual signalling components required per 9.10.19.1.
notes: Accessory-unit alarm package driver.

question: What fire separation is required between a basement apartment and the rest of the house?
reference_answer: OBC 9.10.9 requires walls and floors that must be fire separations to be built as continuous barriers against fire and smoke (9.10.9.2), and it governs smoke-tight barriers in houses with a secondary suite. There is targeted relief: floor assemblies contained within a dwelling unit or within a house with a secondary suite need not be constructed as fire separations (9.10.9.13), which is why suite-boundary assemblies and closures (9.10.13) carry the requirement instead.
notes: Suite-boundary driver for accessory-unit drafts.

question: What is the minimum ceiling height for a basement apartment?
reference_answer: OBC 9.5.3.1: ceiling heights in secondary suites must be at least 1.95 m, with clear height under beams and ducting at least 1.85 m. Other residential rooms follow Table 9.5.3.1 (for example, living/dining/kitchen spaces need 2,300 mm over at least 75% of the required floor area), and the conforming area must be contiguous with the room's entry.
notes: Feasibility flag threshold in guideline S6.2 references 9.5.3 minimums.

question: What are the maximum rise and minimum run allowed for basement stairs?
reference_answer: Per OBC 9.8.4.1/9.8.4.2 (Table 9.8.4.1), private stairs — interior stairs within a house with a secondary suite or a dwelling unit — allow a maximum rise of 200 mm, minimum rise of 125 mm, maximum run of 355 mm, and minimum run of 255 mm, measured nosing to nosing.

question: When is a handrail required on a basement stair?
reference_answer: OBC 9.8.7.1 requires handrails on stairs and ramps per Table 9.8.7.1, but stairs serving a single dwelling unit are exempt when interior stairs have no more than 2 risers (3 for exterior). Only one handrail is required on exterior stairs of more than 3 risers serving one dwelling unit or a house with a secondary suite.

question: What building code requirements apply when converting a basement into a legal second unit?
reference_answer: OBC Section 9.41 (Additional Requirements for Change of Use) applies when construction changes the use of all or part of an existing building, including creating a second dwelling unit. It triggers compensating construction so the converted space conforms to the listed Part 9 requirements (room dimensions, means of egress, windows, and related subsections referenced by 9.41.2.1). The 2024 numbering places the suite-conversion trigger at 9.41.
notes: Suite-conversion trigger; pairs with zoning 4.19 in accessory-unit drafts.

question: What sound insulation is required between a basement apartment and the main dwelling?
reference_answer: OBC 9.11.1.1: a dwelling unit must be separated from every other space where noise may be generated either by an assembly plus adjoining construction achieving an apparent sound transmission class (ASTC) of at least 47, or by a separating assembly rated at least STC 50 with adjoining constructions conforming to 9.11.1.4.
notes: Why the Sonopan/resilient-channel add-on exists in quote exclusions.

question: Is a basement apartment (additional residential unit) allowed in a detached house in Cambridge?
reference_answer: Yes — By-law 26-007 s.4.19(a) permits additional residential units in a detached house, semi-detached house, or street townhouse dwelling on a parcel of urban residential land, subject to the by-law's requirements. The ARU must be on the same lot as the principal dwelling, and where municipal water and sewer services are available both dwellings must connect to them.
notes: Core ARU permission; eval accessory-unit scenarios retrieve this.

question: How many additional residential units can I add on my lot in Cambridge?
reference_answer: By-law 26-007 s.4.19(d) caps the count: the permitted combinations include one attached ARU plus one detached ARU on the same lot as the principal dwelling. ARUs are not permitted within or on the same lot as a group home (s.4.19(e)).

question: Do I need an extra parking space for a basement apartment in Cambridge?
reference_answer: Yes — By-law 26-007 s.4.19(f) requires one additional parking space per ARU, and that space may be a tandem space. No new driveway or vehicular access from the lot to a street is permitted for the purpose of providing ARU access or parking.

question: What are the siting rules for a detached additional residential unit in Cambridge?
reference_answer: By-law 26-007 s.4.19.2: a detached ARU may be located in the interior side yard, exterior side yard, or rear yard, with a minimum 1.2 m setback from the interior side lot line, an exterior side setback matching the principal dwelling's requirement, and a minimum 1.2 m rear lot line setback.
notes: Capstone-adjacent (detached ARU) but a clean single-section retrieval target.

question: What is the minimum front yard setback for a detached house in Cambridge's R2 zone?
reference_answer: Table 7.3A of By-law 26-007 (s.7.3 Zone Standards) sets the minimum required front yard for a detached dwelling at 3.0 m in the R2 zone (6.0 m in RR and R1), with a minimum 8.0 m front yard to a garage and a 9.0 m minimum lot frontage in R2.
notes: Table-lookup case — tests that tabular zone standards survive chunking.

question: Is a portable toilet included in the quote?
reference_answer: Quoting rule 5.14: a portable toilet is included at $2,000 if the client will not provide bathroom access during construction. This is a GROUNDED value from Company A's real contract boilerplate.
notes: Small, unambiguous rule lookup.

question: How must excluded or capped items be written in a quote?
reference_answer: Quoting rule 5.18: excluded or capped items must state count and location explicitly — for example 'Kitchen Center Island (Upstairs & Downstairs)' rather than 'Kitchen Center Island', and 'up to 6 LNFT of cabinets' rather than 'cabinets'. The rule was mined from the _REVISED quote pairs, where an ambiguous exclusion survived a first draft and forced a revision.
notes: The revised-pairs-derived rule; eval Q7 support.

question: What does a finished basement typically cost per square foot?
reference_answer: Guideline S8 price anchors: a finished basement runs roughly $45-65 per sqft and an accessory unit roughly $75-130 per sqft (placeholder band fitted to grounded points — smaller GFA drives higher $/sqft because kitchen, bath, and entrance costs don't scale down). Real anchors include a SUPERIOR 1,563 sqft finished basement at $77,500 (about $50/sqft) and a SUPREME 745 sqft legal suite at $94,950 (about $127/sqft).
notes: Sanity band for drafted totals.

question: What is the quartz countertop allowance for each package tier?
reference_answer: The material-allowances table (kitchen category, GROUNDED in real 2026 quotes) sets the quartz countertop allowance at $30/sqft for ESSENTIAL and $45/sqft for SUPERIOR and SUPREME; SUPREME also extends quartz to the backsplash at up to $45/sqft.
notes: CSV chunk — section_number is the CSV group key, not a numeric section.

question: When must the assistant stop drafting and route the request to the human estimator?
reference_answer: Guideline S6.1 lists the hard-route triggers that end drafting immediately: out-of-scope project types (new builds, additions, garden/laneway suites, commercial), structural work, hazardous or damaged sites, insurance/restoration claims, permit avoidance, legalizing unpermitted work, zoning approvals beyond by-right, legacy electrical/servicing, tenancy complications, contract-term changes, GFA under 400 or over 2,500 sqft, and unrealistic budgets or timelines. Hard route beats flag (S6.3): any single hard trigger ends drafting even if every slot is filled.
notes: Eval Q6 anchor; source of truth for trigger routing.

reference_answer: The corpus has two real accessory-unit conversions: P11 (ESSENTIAL tier, Milton) and P20 (SUPREME tier, Milton, $94,950 for 745 sqft including drawings and permit). P19 included a kitchenette/wet bar, a full bathroom plus powder room, and SUPERIOR-tier finishes (AGT/painted-MDF cabinetry, $45/sqft quartz allowance, LVP flooring).

question: What items does Company A typically exclude from a basement quote?
reference_answer: Standard exclusions listed on real quotes include: permits and city fees, minor-variance approvals, municipal parking fees, landscaping/driveway/porch work, glass railings and pickets, appliances and their installation, feature walls/fireplaces, ceiling soundproofing (resilient channel + Sonopan) as an add-on, DMX-plus-plywood subfloor upgrade, heated floors, EV charger rough-in, closet organizers, water-infiltration repair, and duct trunk relocation.
notes: Boilerplate-block retrieval: matches any quote's EXCLUSIONS chunk by section title.
